newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thousand delegates attend Algerian party founding.
newsitem.headline: Thousand delegates attend Algerian party founding.

text.p: Around 1,100 delegates attended a founding congress on Thursday of Algeria's new National Democratic Rally party.
The party, formed less than two months ago, is chaired by Abdelkader Bensalah, a staunch ally of Algerian President Liamine Zeroual.
It is seen by many Algerian commentators as having staked out a strong position ahead of parliamentary elections due, after five years of violence and political unrest, on June 5.

Bensalah said the party responded to the "profound aspirations of reuniting Algerians in an organised framework, conscious of the challenges and objectives to bring Algeria out of this difficult situation."
His speech was reported by the official Algerian news agency APS.
Bensalah said the party would draw up a manifesto of "concrete proposals on questions linked to economic and social fronts, on the rational exploitation and use" of resources.
The NDR leader said Algeria's economic reforms -- switching to a free market after nearly three decades of centralised control -- were irreversible.
He said the party would answer the expectations of Algeria's 29 million people for "security, stability and economic and social prosperity."
About 60,000 people have been killed since Algerian authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which the fundamentalist Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.
Algeria has since been without an elected parliament but has had an appointed body, the Transitional National Council, of which Bensalah was head, to examine laws.
